title: Precision Pathway Advisor and Safety Checks for Hybrid Quantization
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime component (Precision Pathway Advisor) that selects candidate mixed-precision execution lanes (FP16/FP8/INT8) per-request or per-batch using precomputed quantization profiles, and enforces fast safety checks using calibration metrics and a compact accuracy guard. This ticket covers design, calibration dataset pipeline integration, validation harness, telemetry hooks, and a staged rollout plan with rollback criteria.

Scope:
- Define a compact quant-profile descriptor used at runtime (per-layer scale ranges, outlier stats, dynamic range, per-op quant suitability score).
- Integrate with existing calibration pipeline to emit descriptors for FP8 and INT8 profiles.
- Build Advisor module that consumes descriptor, request characteristics (seq length, sampling temperature, user tier), and returns ranked lanes + expected latency/cost delta and an accuracy risk estimate.
- Add safety checks: sample-based quick-validate (N=32 per-model minibatch) using cached eval prompts and a threshold-driven accept/reject.
- Add telemetry: per-request advisor decision, chosen lane, safety-check result, and offline accuracy regression alerts.

Non-goals: full retraining or model finetune for quantization, heavy per-request calibration, or changing kernel implementations here. Those remain in inference-runtime and quantization teams.

Success criteria:
- Advisor returns decision in <0.5ms (median) added overhead for hot paths.
- No more than 0.5% top-line accuracy regression on holdout evals vs FP16 baseline after canary.
- Telemetry exposes per-lane latency and end-to-end quality regressions within 1h of occurrence.

Links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Precision+Pathway+Advisor, Calibration pipeline spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quant+Calibration, initial proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1498
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ethan Park: Created ticket. Initial architecture sketch uploaded to Confluence. Decided to keep advisor stateless and rely on precomputed descriptors to avoid extra storage/consensus complexity.

2026-03-11 - Marisol Vega: Ran microbenchmarks for descriptor size (per-layer 128-byte target); FP8 profiles with dynamic range + 2-percentile outlier stats fit comfortably. Adding small per-model checksum to detect stale descriptors.

2026-03-11 - Arjun Singh (review): Flag: Quick-validate minibatch must be sampled from production-like prompts to be meaningful. Suggested: use stratified sample across top-10 user prompt buckets. Also suggested a configurable budget for validation (default 32).

2026-03-12 - Marisol Vega: Implemented prototype Advisor decision function. Candidate ranking includes: expected latency delta (ms), cost delta ($/k tokens), accuracy risk score computed from calibration divergence metric. Prototype returns top-2 lanes for fallback wiring. Benchmarks: added ~0.38ms median per-infer overhead in our synthetic harness. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1507

2026-03-12 - QA notes: Quick-validate harness shows occasional false positives when prompts contain long numerical tables. Plan: extend validation set to include 10% structured/table prompts. Also add tolerance relaxation for numeric tokens (relative error vs absolute).

2026-03-12 - Product feedback (Nora Li): Ensure we expose 'advisor_reason' in response metadata for debugging and for customers on Dedicated. Keep default behavior conservative for enterprise customers (prefer FP16 unless explicit override).
